title: Why the founder of a regional incubator is stepping away
text: The weeks founders spend in these programmes are too short, and the sessions are often improvised or lack a clear plan. Many rely on volunteers who drop in to speak to startups a couple of hours a month, which he found wasn’t enough time to change much for the founders. On top of that, because many incubators have quotas to fill in each cohort, they take on teams whose ideas are weaker than they should be.

title: An Incubator Is Not an Accelerator
text:
Last spring, I saw a founder make a choice that will probably sink their company. They signed up for an “accelerator” that was, in practice, an incubator dressed up in an accelerator’s branding. Five months later, they’re burning runway on workshops built for a company at an entirely different stage.

Calling every programme an “accelerator” actively hurts founders by hiding the real difference between what a company needs at each stage of its life.

Theory doesn’t help at this stage. Templates don’t help. You need mentors who have taken these calls under the same pressure you’re under. The best programme mentors carry scars, and they’ve paid for the mistakes.

title: Why foreign founders should think twice about a big startup campus
text: Although Hangar Nord says English is its working language, more than 60% of its events and workshops are run in French only. This is especially true for sessions hosted by public agencies such as the regional business office, the very team that is supposed to help everyone (foreigners included) set up a company in France.

title: Un accelerateur londonien quitte a son tour Paris
text:
L’ antenne parisienne de l’accélérateur londonien, installée sur le campus Hangar Nord, va donc fermer ses portes.

Cette décision n’est pas vraiment une surprise, dans la mesure où Rampart Ventures, accélérateur américain connu, a lui aussi choisi cette année de fermer ses bureaux de Paris et de Berlin.

title: Our insurance startup moves out of the campus: honest feedback
text:
No need to leave our desks: all the VCs come to Hangar Nord. Northfold, Brightwater, Kelp Capital, Ondine Partners, and also Larchmont, Thistle and Saltmarsh regularly visit the building.

This proximity saves a huge amount of time and, above all, is a rare opportunity during a growth phase.

All in all, Hangar Nord has been a fantastic catalyst that let us save 6 months of work and thanks to which we can now claim to be a credible player on the European insurance market. After the wave of neo-banks across Europe, get ready for the neo-insurers, with Parasol in the front row 💪
